name: Digicam 2005
description: Mid-2000s compact digital camera: tiny sensor, deep focus, crunchy sharpening, JPEG blocking.
rationale: A 1/2.5" sensor (5.76 mm wide) at f/2.8 behaves like f/16+ on full frame — deep DOF comes from the real sensor crop and a forced minimum f-stop on the CAMERA, never from fake blur. In-camera processing oversharpened aggressively (halo radius ~2 px at 5 MP). CCD shadow noise is chroma-dominant (blotchy color, not luma grain). Highlights clip hard in sensor RGB before white balance, leaving a magenta/pink cast in blown skies. 4:1:1-ish JPEG chroma subsampling plus 8x8 DCT gives faint blocking. High-contrast edges show purple fringing from axial chromatic aberration and sensor blooming.
